builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging
summary: The framework replaces uncalibrated Bayesian M/EEG source estimates (BMN+sLORETA, SBL) with posterior calibration via isotonic recalibration of credible-region levels using empirical coverage. It costs simulation-based calibration runs and closed-form posterior computation, with complexity in evidence-maximization noise learning and post-hoc recalibration. It can fail through residual miscalibration that persists after recalibration, and transfer of calibration across mismatched SNR, sparsity, or head models is condition dependent.
rationale: The method targets neuroimaging inverse problems for M/EEG source localization, which is unrelated to LLM inference, training, agent systems, or any production concern of an AI/ML engineer with constrained infrastructure.
technique: Bayesian uncertainty calibration for M/EEG source imaging

claims.statement: The framework replaces uncalibrated Bayesian M/EEG source estimates (BMN+sLORETA, SBL) with posterior calibration via isotonic recalibration of credible-region levels using empirical coverage. It costs simulation-based calibration runs and closed-form posterior computation, with complexity in evidence-maximization noise learning and post-hoc recalibration. It can fail through residual miscalibration that persists after recalibration, and transfer of calibration across mismatched SNR, sparsity, or head models is condition dependent.

SBL+S-FLEX yields lower Wasserstein localization error, smaller posterior uncertainty, and coverage closer to nominal credibility than BMN+sLORETA before recalibration; isotonic recalibration improves both methods.
